column1: # `canon v` renders any value as canonical AQL source — the same
# renderer (eng.CanonValue) the spec suites and the doc-example
# harness compare against. For DATA values (scalars, atoms, paths,
# none, type literals, plain and flex Node trees) the result is
# ROUND-TRIPPABLE: evaluating it reproduces an equivalent value, with
# flexness marked at every level. Identity-bearing values (Array,
# Store, instances, functions) render too, but rebuilding from source
# yields a FRESH container — only data round-trips, not identity.
# NOTE on expectations: the spec runner itself canon-renders the
# result stack, and canon returns a String — so the expected fields
# below are the canon rendering OF that string (one extra quote layer).

column3: atoms render in /q form (a bare name would re-parse as a word)
type literals render as their name
an ordinary string keeps the single-quoted form

column1: # §2  string quoting is chosen so the output RE-PARSES: content with a
#     single quote switches to double quotes; content with both kinds
#     which re-parsed wrongly — canon was not round-trippable for it.

column3: single quote in content → double-quoted output
double quote in content → single-quoted output
both kinds + backslash → escaped single-quoted output

column1: # §3  Node trees — flexness is marked at every level

column3: an entirely-flex tree is (flex …) all the way down
a literal-embedded live handle is visible in the rendering

column1: # §4  round-trips: evaluating the canon string reproduces the value
import "aql:vm" def v (flex {a:[1]}) (Vm.run (canon v)) deq v
import "aql:vm" def s "it's \"q\" \\ ok" (Vm.run (canon s)) eq s
